subject.title: feat(onboarding): unified empty-state with provider icons, websites, and recommended installs

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently curate a static cross-vendor install catalog, or should onboarding recommendations come only from provider/plugin discovery contracts that can produce an actionable setup route?
rationale: The branch adds lasting core product policy and a public plugin metadata contract; code review cannot determine which vendors core should endorse or what activation guarantees a recommendation must provide.

options.title: Derive actionable recommendations
options.body: Require provider/plugin-owned discovery metadata and emit only recommendations whose install, authentication, or activation path OpenClaw can explain and subsequently detect.

options.title: Sponsor the core catalog
options.body: Keep the nine-entry catalog as explicit core policy, but add per-tool prerequisite/action metadata and maintain a tested activation contract for every entry.

options.title: Land metadata without recommendations
options.body: Ship the icon and website presentation plumbing while deferring the static recommendation catalog until its ownership and activation semantics are agreed.

recommendation.title: Derive actionable recommendations
recommendation.body: Require provider/plugin-owned discovery metadata and emit only recommendations whose install, authentication, or activation path OpenClaw can explain and subsequently detect.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns onboarding product policy and the related first-run provider direction this person has been driving.
